dynnikov_coordinates — DRIVE braidpath op

• Data kinds: signal × scalar → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.dynnikov_coordinates(word, n_strands) (to call the implementation directly, import braidpath; braidpath.dynnikov_coordinates(word, n_strands); from the registry, opsdrive.get("dynnikov_coordinates"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Dynnikov coordinates of the braid acting on the standard curve diagram E = (0, …, 0; −1, …, −1) (integers, no overflow).

Taken on the disk with n + 1 punctures: the n strands plus one extra puncture at the right end (a and b both have length n − 1). This action is faithful, so coordinates equal ⇔ same braid. Each letter needs only a constant number of additions/subtractions and max / min, so the time is proportional to the word length (unlike handle reduction or free-group images, nothing swells —— the numbers only get larger, and Python integers do not overflow).

Returns: dict a, b (lists of int), key (tuple a + b, used as the class key), n_strands, n_punctures, max_abs (largest absolute value of the coordinates), bits.

Empty input (word with 0 elements) returns the coordinates of the standard curve diagram (reason: the empty word is the identity and does not move the curve diagram).
